greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. We gather today in the presence of the angels and the saints, seeking the light of the Lord who sees us exactly where we are.
penitential: Lord Jesus, you are the King of heaven and earth: Lord, have mercy. Lord Jesus, you see us in our secret places and know our hearts: Christ, have mercy. Lord Jesus, you promise us that we will see the heavens opened: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: In the sight of the angels I will sing your praises, Lord.
homily:
We often imagine the spiritual life as a climb—a slow, arduous ascent up a mountain, trying to reach a God who is hidden somewhere in the clouds. We think that if we are quiet enough, if we are pious enough, if we are good enough, we might finally catch a glimpse of the divine. But the readings today, on this feast of the Archangels, flip that perspective entirely. They suggest that the movement of grace is not us climbing toward God, but God descending toward us, and the angels, those messengers of His constant presence, are the ones who bridge the distance.

Look at the Prophet Daniel in our first reading. He sees a vision of the Ancient One, a throne of fire, a surging stream of light. It is a terrifying, majestic, overwhelming sight. But then, the vision shifts. He sees 'one like a son of man' coming on the clouds. It is a moment of arrival. It is a moment where the infinite reaches down to touch the finite. And then, move to the Gospel. Nathanael is sitting under a fig tree—a place of shade, a place of quiet, a place of private thought. He is just existing, just being, perhaps wondering about the world, perhaps wondering about the promises of God. And Jesus speaks those piercing words: 'Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.'

I want you to sit with that for a moment. 'I saw you.' It is the most beautiful thing one human being can say to another, and it is the most beautiful thing God says to us. It means you are not hidden. It means your grief, your joy, your questions, your late-night prayers, your early-morning memories of your son—none of it is invisible to Him. Jesus saw Nathanael before he even knew he was being watched. He sees you, Alan, and you, Thao, in the quiet of your home. He sees you, Ryan, in the moments when you carry the weight of being a brother, when you look at the world and feel the absence of your best friend.

Benjamin was a boy who understood that the world was full of these hidden connections. He was a boy of brilliant, analytical depth—he could look at a complex AWS environment or a line of code and see the logic beneath the surface. He had that sharp, beautiful mind that wanted to know how things worked, how they fit together, how they took flight. But he also had a heart that was remarkably, tenderly open. Think of that moment when he offered his entire piggy bank to help his uncle. He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it, he didn't need to make a spectacle of his charity. The offer itself was the truth of his soul. It was a heart that looked at the suffering of another and immediately wanted to give everything it had. That is the heart of a saint. That is the heart that Jesus saw under the fig tree.

I know that for you, these last three months have felt like a long, quiet season under a different kind of tree. You are sitting in the shade of a great loss, and the silence can feel absolute. You wonder if God is seeing you, or if the heavens have closed. But the promise of today’s Gospel is the opposite: 'You will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.' Heaven is not a distant country; it is a reality that is constantly breaking into our lives. When you feel a sudden, warm memory of Ben’s smile, that is a grace. When you see a bird in flight—that creature he loved so much—and it reminds you of his dream of 'con chim airlines,' that is a messenger. When you gather as a family, even when the table feels incomplete, the very fact that you are still loving each other, still holding on, is a sign that the angels are at work in your home.

There is a temptation to think that because a life was short, it was somehow unfinished. We measure life by the calendar, by the years, by the milestones we expected to see. But God measures life by the capacity to love. Benjamin’s life was not a broken flight plan; it was a life that arrived exactly where it was meant to be. He is at the Banquet of Heaven. He is standing in the presence of the Ancient One, and he is doing exactly what the Psalm says: 'In the sight of the angels, I will sing your praises.' He is singing. He is whole. He is seeing the very things he used to dream about—not from the ground, but from the heart of the light itself.

I want to speak very gently to the ache that sometimes visits you in the dark. There is a weight that parents often carry, a stone of 'what if' or 'did I miss something.' I want to lift that stone from you today. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were his sanctuary. You were the ones who nurtured that brilliant, curious, gentle spirit. You did not miss anything. God does not look at your son’s life and find it lacking, and He does not look at your care for him and find it wanting. You are not being accused. You are being held. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the burden of self-reproach. That is a weight that has no place in the kingdom of God.

Ryan, you are the keeper of the memory. You are the one who knows the rhythm of his giggles, the way he looked when he was focused on a game, the way he shared the world with you. When you feel lonely, do not think of yourself as a brother who is left behind. Think of yourself as a brother who is carrying his light forward. Every time you are kind, every time you are curious, every time you choose to build something beautiful, you are honoring him. You are the bridge. You are the one who shows the world that love is not a memory—it is a living, breathing force that continues to shape the future.

We are on the feast of the Archangels—Michael, who defends; Gabriel, who announces; Raphael, who heals. These are the ones who stand in the presence of God and move between heaven and earth. They are the ones who are watching over Benjamin, and they are the ones who are watching over you. They are the ones who make sure that the connection is never broken. When the world feels too heavy, when the 'why' feels too big to hold, stop trying to find the answer in the logic of the world. Look for the presence in the 'Who.' The Who is Jesus. He is the one who saw Nathanael, and He is the one who sees you. He is the one who is even now preparing a place for you to be reunited with your son in a joy that will never, ever end.

Take this with you today: you are a family of four, and that will never change. The geography of your life has shifted, but the bond of your love is eternal. Keep the 'Well of Love' flowing in his name. Keep the kindness moving. Keep the dream alive. And when you walk out those doors, look up at the sky. Remember that he is not in the dust. He is in the light. He is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile. You are never walking alone. You are being led, step by step, home to the One who loves you more than you can imagine. Amen.
petitions: For Benjamin Vo, that he may rest in the light of Christ and enjoy the fullness of the Banquet of Heaven, we pray to the Lord.
For all who grieve, especially Alan, Thao, and Ryan, that the Lord may console them, strengthen their hearts, and give them the peace of His presence, we pray to the Lord.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, may He let His face shine upon you and be gracious to you, and may He give you His peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: For a boy named Ben and all who have died, that they rest in the light of Christ.
For all who grieve, that God console them and give them hope.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
As I watched:



Thrones were set up

and the Ancient One took his throne.

His clothing was bright as snow,

and the hair on his head as white as wool;

His throne was flames of fire,

with wheels of burning fire.

A surging stream of fire

flowed out from where he sat;

Thousands upon thousands were ministering to him,

and myriads upon myriads attended him.



The court was convened, and the books were opened.

As the visions during the night continued, I saw



One like a son of man coming,

on the clouds of heaven;

When he reached the Ancient One

and was presented before him,

He received dominion, glory, and kingship;

nations and peoples of every language serve him.

His dominion is an everlasting dominion

that shall not be taken away,

his kingship shall not be destroyed.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (1) In the sight of the angels I will sing your praises, Lord.

I will give thanks to you, O LORD, with all my heart,

for you have heard the words of my mouth;

in the presence of the angels I will sing your praise;

I will worship at your holy temple

and give thanks to your name.

R. In the sight of the angels I will sing your praises, Lord.

Because of your kindness and your truth;

for you have made great above all things

your name and your promise.

When I called, you answered me;

you built up strength within me.

R. In the sight of the angels I will sing your praises, Lord.

All the kings of the earth shall give thanks to you, O LORD

when they hear the words of your mouth;

And they shall sing of the ways of the LORD

"Great is the glory of the LORD

R. In the sight of the angels I will sing your praises, Lord.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said of him,

"Here is a true child of Israel.

There is no duplicity in him."

Nathanael said to him, "How do you know me?"

Jesus answered and said to him,

"Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree."

Nathanael answered him,

"Rabbi, you are the Son of God; you are the King of Israel."

Jesus answered and said to him,

"Do you believe

because I told you that I saw you under the fig tree?

You will see greater things than this."

And he said to him, "Amen, amen, I say to you,

you will see heaven opened

and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man."

day: Feast of Saints Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael, Archangels

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.

Ben ơi, Làm cả ngày tới tối, đến lúc chuẩn bị đi ngủ thì nằm một lúc lại nhớ Ben, nhớ mấy chuyện hai anh em từng nói với nhau. Nghĩ tới em, anh thấy buồn nhiều lắm. Ben hãy luôn theo dõi và cầu nguyện cho ba mẹ và Ryan nhé, nước mắt chảy ngược nó khủng khiếp hơn chảy xuôi đó Ben.

Ben ơi, ba nhớ con nhiều quá.

Mommy cũng vậy. Hơn hai tháng rồi mà ba má vẫn khóc mỗi ngày.

Con giúp ba má vượt qua nha, để lo cho em
